newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy will keep 97 deficit to 3 pct - Macciotta.
newsitem.headline: Italy will keep 97 deficit to 3 pct - Macciotta.

text.p: Italy will take further corrective measures if the 1997 budget deficit turns out at the end of the year to have exceeded three percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), a junior government minister said on Tuesday.

Budget Ministry undersecretary Giorgio Macciotta noted in a speech in parliament that European Union estimates were of a budget deficit of 3.2 percent, just above the 3.0 percent target required for membership of Europe's planned single currency.
The 0.2 percent of GDP was equivalent to four trillion lire, he told the Senate (upper house).
"It is such a ridiculous figure that if there were this difference there would be no lack of instruments to propose a correction to parliament to eliminate this margin," he said.

He was speaking during a debate on a supplementary budget of 15.5 trillion lire which the government has presented to parliament to try to ensure Italy stays inside the deficit-to-GDP ratio required for economic and monetary union.
Macciotta later told reporters that the government had no evidence that the 1997 deficit would exceed three percent.
"It would be impossible to assess it at this time because the figure is so small that it is impossible to foresee in advance," he said.
